principle: Lane C original classifications are not rewritten. This file adds the CP7 integration disposition per surface and the closure counts. Lane C docs-only status is preserved (runtime diff of Lane C = 0).

closure_summary.potential_surface: CP7A-014 (forged coverage snapshot / forged ApprovalReference threat at Brain ExecutionPlan construction).
closure_mechanism: 1. Eligibility for executable state comes only from the CP6 server-owned guard path: EvidenceEligibilityService materializes evidence from Guard-run output; callers can never pass coverage, guard_run_id or a guard fake (authorization-service test: caller cannot inject evidence coverage / forged guard_run_id cannot materialize coverage).

2. The cross-language ApprovalBindingPayload binds the exact evidence_coverage_digest that is part of the server-owned ExecutionPlan; it deliberately does NOT claim native re-proof of the CP6 GuardRunStore lineage (cp7-approval-binding-contract.json section 5).

3. A caller can never set required_approval, risk_snapshot or state=ready (strict request schema + server-owned lifecycle); a bare ApprovalReference can never ready a plan (verifier requires a real native grant).

4. The reference is not an authority: native approval authority comes exclusively from the persistent ApprovalStore record (approval_id + plan_id + token_reference + token_digest + policy_version + binding_digest + actor + authority + status + expiry all validated); fabricated references are rejected.
5. No public approval mutation IPC and no generic execute IPC exist (execute_ipc_enabled=false; the only broker IPC is read-only status).
6. CP9 bridge requirement recorded: any future Brain->Tauri bridge must submit the server-owned ExecutionPlan/approval lifecycle object, never a caller-constructed plan.
closure_summary.residual: None. The threat is closed by authority-boundary design plus the native store authority; no code path lets a caller-constructed plan with forged coverage or a forged reference reach spawn.

surfaces.detail: CP7 replaced the blanket PlanRejectedApproval gate with a real Approval Authority consult: store record lookup (approval_id, plan_id, token_reference, token_digest, policy_version, binding_digest, actor, authority, status, expiry), native minimum risk policy, expiry, single-use consume, and a durable plan ledger. Crash-safe sequencing is accept -> reserve -> consume -> spawn (fault points BeforePlanReserve/AfterPlanReserve/BeforeApprovalConsume/AfterApprovalConsume/BeforeSpawn).

surfaces.detail: The runner remains the single private spawn path and is reached only after the approval authority accepted the plan and durably consumed the grant. Spawn failure never unconsumes the approval nor unreserves the plan.

No approve/execute/grant command is registered; the Tauri handler set gained no approval mutation command in CP7.

surfaces.detail: Binding registration stays internal/trusted (Rust bootstrap only). CP7 adds no IPC registration path; production bindings remain the five read-only github.* bindings.
Compiled capability catalog unchanged by CP7; the approval authority reads the compiled binding as the native minimum source of truth.
The wire reference carries only opaque fields; the authority is the persistent store record. Execution validates every reference field against the stored grant (constant-time digest comparison).
Schema validity confers no authority; the authorization service requires ApprovalGrantVerifier PASS (fake verifier success/failure covered). Bare references can never ready a plan.
required_approval, risk_snapshot, state and approval are server-owned; strict request schema rejects caller-supplied values. Plan construction goes through the authorization service.
CP6 eligibility remains the only evidence qualification authority; CP7 binds its exact coverage digest and does not re-prove lineage natively.
Cancel remains an execution-lifecycle control; it cannot undo a consumed approval or a reserved plan.
No public approve/grant/revoke/deny command was added in CP7; CP9 will design the owner interaction.
